transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-17
Start: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~82 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Omar Reyes, Priya Patel, Jason Li, Ella Novak, Samir Gupta

Summary (auto): quick triage of late regression hits in staging; define staging fallback playbook; identify observability gaps in routing/caching; assign owners for runbook + regression harness.

[00:00:02] Maya Chen: ok, uh, thanks everyone for joining — try to keep this tight. We saw the regression alerts overnight in staging, and we need to get a fallback runbook in place before the next canary.
[00:00:18] Omar Reyes: yeah the alert fired around 02:14 staging region, queueing spiked and a bunch of requests hit the slow path. It looked like memory climbed and we started dropping KV cache entries, which cascaded into longer latencies.
[00:00:35] Priya Patel: to be precise, it wasn't the kv cache eviction we normally expect; there were a few places the transcription shows K V cash — um, the trace shows prefix cache misses correlated with a new kernel fallback that rolled out yesterday.
[00:00:50] Jason Li: oh right — the kernel fallback patch we pushed to prod-staging was meant to reduce tail latency but we suspected it might nudge memory pressure up.
[00:01:05] Ella Novak: QA started seeing intermittent OOM-ish restarts on a couple of nodes, not consistently reproducible. We do have a reproduction run that sometimes fails but it's flaky.
[00:01:20] Maya Chen: cool — agenda for the hour: 1) quick incident synthesis, 2) agree fallback playbook for staging (what switches, who pages), 3) observability gaps to close before next canary, 4) action items.

[00:02:05] Omar: quick synthesis — sequence was deploy -> elevated mem usage -> prefix cache drop -> routing to slower kernels -> higher per-token CPU and memory -> queueing -> request timeouts. There was also an increase in model reroutes to a lower-capacity pool that made it worse.
[00:02:28] Priya: I think the critical bit is the interaction between kernel selection and prefix cache sizing. The kernel selection logic picked a variant that has higher KV footprint; combined with a rare input pattern increased the KV footprint beyond the expected distribution.
[00:02:45] Samir Gupta: can we reproduce with a stress harness that targets large prefix lengths? I tried a few synthetic prompts but didn't get the same OOM.
[00:02:59] Ella: we ran the customer-like prompt list and only saw failures when we force token-window to 2048 in the harness; otherwise it's fine.
[00:03:13] Maya: okay so reproduction is possible but needs a specific token distribution. That makes it high-risk for canary because production traffic might trigger it rarely.

[00:04:00] Jason: about the runbook — suggestion: a staged fallback policy: 1) if queueing > threshold AND mem > 80% -> flip kernel to lower-memory quantized variant for new requests; 2) disable some non-essential batching optimizations; 3) if condition persists, route a % of traffic to Dedicated pool or smaller model; 4) if production-like impact, rollback the kernel.
[00:04:26] Priya: caution — switching kernels mid-request is unsafe; we can only route new requests to different kernel. We need to ensure KV cache warmup won't make things worse.
[00:04:40] Omar: agree. Also need to add a cool-down timer: don't keep flipping every minute. A 10-min window makes sense.
[00:04:51] Maya: ok, document those constraints. Who will own the actual runbook?
[00:04:56] Jason: I can own drafting the runbook structure (ops steps + decision tree), but Maya should own sign-off.
[00:05:04] Maya: fine. Jason then.

[00:05:25] Priya: observability gaps — top of list: 1) we do not have a metric that directly ties prefix-cache hits to kernel selection events; 2) traces are missing correlation IDs in the kernel selection layer; 3) alerting currently watches per-node mem but not queue latency per model-route.
[00:05:48] Omar: yeah, alerting is too coarse. We need a composite alert: model-route queue > X AND cache_miss_rate > Y for > 3mins. Otherwise false positives.
[00:06:03] Ella: QA also flagged that logs sometimes obfuscate which model variant answered — logs say "quantized" or "fallback" but the metadata field is often empty because the runtime didn't populate it in the crash path.
[00:06:18] Priya: oh that's from a try/catch in the handler — we swallow metadata on error. That's on me. I'll fix it.
[00:06:25] Samir: from release perspective, we need gating: any kernel changes should include a canary checklist that includes the prefix-length regression harness.

[00:06:50] Maya: ok, proposed playbook bullets: - detection thresholds (queueing + mem + cache miss) - immediate mitigation (route new requests to lower-memory variant, disable heavy batching) - stabilization (monitor 10 min, warmup cache) - escalation (pager to SRE and release) - rollback criteria. Add those to runbook.
[00:07:12] Omar: add a step to fail open to a simpler model when latency hits SLO breaches for >5 minutes; that gives better user experience than 100% errors.
[00:07:24] Jason: I'm noting that. Also include channels — Slack ops-channel, status page prefilled messages, and who sends an update to sales if customer-facing incidents are likely.

[00:07:45] Priya: re: tracing — we lack end-to-end trace ids for the routing decision. I propose we add a lightweight header that persists through the runtime and kernels — even if sampled — so we can see the kernel selection path in traces.
[00:08:03] Omar: and correlate it with the autoscaler decision logs; that will tell us if autoscaler got triggered in response.
[00:08:12] Maya: perfect. Priya and Omar, you'll own the observability instrumentation.

[00:08:40] Ella: QA action: produce a non-flaky replication by constructing a prompt set that forces long prefix sequences with certain token distributions. I'll attach the failing run and mark the seeds.
[00:08:55] Samir: I'll spin up a small 2-GPU fleet with the exact kernel variant and run the harness overnight. If we reproduce, we'll capture heap profiles.

[00:09:22] (small crosstalk)
[00:09:40] Maya: ok, timeline — we want the runbook and basic alerts in place before we unfreeze the kernel rollout; that's 48 hours ideally. If we can't, we should hold the rollout.
[00:09:56] Omar: I can add the composite alert within the next 24 hours.
[00:10:04] Priya: instrumentation will take longer — maybe 4-5 days to get solid trace coverage. But we can add a short-term metric: instrument the kernel selection event counter and emit a tag for kernel_variant. That should be 1-2 days.

[00:10:30] Jason: note on communications: we should let the oncall know about the fallback behavior and runbook changes; and update the runbook publishing to include the exact paging policy.

[00:11:05] Maya: great. any blockers?
[00:11:10] Ella: we need access to the staging logs stored in the long-term S3 bucket; current QA cluster can't pull those easily due to IAM restrictions.
[00:11:20] Samir: I'll audit and open a ticket to grant QA read access for the bucket.

[00:11:40] Priya: one more item — quantized model variant has slightly different latency profile; routing a percent of traffic to it may change cost per token. We should model cost impact in the runbook so PMs can sign off.
[00:11:58] Maya: good point. Jason, can you run a quick delta estimate?
[00:12:05] Jason: yes I can. I'll estimate cost delta for full traffic and for 10% diversion.

[00:12:26] Omar: re: fallback thresholds — let's be specific. Queueing per-route 95th > 800ms AND mem usage > 78% on >=3 nodes for 2 minutes. Then route 20% traffic to fallback variant and disable aggressive batching. If that improves within 10 minutes, keep at 20% for 30 minutes then slowly ramp down.
[00:12:55] Priya: sounds reasonable. We also need a manual knob for Release Eng to flip immediate full rollback.

[00:13:20] Maya: assigning owners recap: Jason runbook doc, Omar alerts and paging policy, Priya kernel telemetry + tag, Samir regression harness, Ella QA replication. Any additions?
[00:13:33] (pause)
[00:13:40] Samir: I'll also gather heap profiles and attach to the runbook when available.

[00:14:05] Maya: ok next — retrospective notes: this leak surfaced because the test matrix didn't include the specific prefix distribution. We should add that to gating for kernel merges. Samir, can you add a gating item to the release checklist?
[00:14:20] Samir: yes will do.

[00:14:35] Priya: on the instrumentation note, one nuance: the model routing code paths are split across two services, and the trace header needs to be passed through the async queue which currently drops some headers. That's a code change requiring coord with infra.
[00:14:51] Omar: infra involvement needed — I'll loop them in.

[00:15:10] Ella: QA will try to reproduce with both async queue and direct call so we can see differences.

[00:15:25] Maya: are we comfortable with the timeline? Short-term (24-48h): runbook draft, composite alert, QA replication ticket, small regression harness. Medium (3-7d): kernel variant telemetry, tracing, full regression run.
[00:15:43] Group: yes/acknowledged (multiple responses overlapped)

[00:16:05] (interruptions, informal chatting)
[00:16:40] Jason: I'll create the runbook skeleton in the ops repo and link it here. I may include a decision tree ascii flow for quick oncall reference.
[00:16:55] Maya: nice. Also, add a quick 'what to say to customers' blurb — short, neutral. We had one customer ping last night and they were confused.
[00:17:08] Omar: aside: we should verify audit logs for who deployed the kernel change and tie to the PR; it's unclear whether the change went through a full gating.
[00:17:20] Samir: I checked — it was auto-merged from a green CI; the gating didn't include the new token-length regression test. I'll take that as a release action.

[00:17:45] Priya: small nit about the cache metric name: in some dashboards it's 'kv_cache_hit' and others it's 'prefix_cache_hit' — standardize.
[00:17:58] Omar: agreed, standardize metrics so alerts work correctly. That's on the observability task.

[00:18:15] Ella: QA will attach the failing seeds and logs to the ticket, expect a link in the next 6 hours.

[00:18:30] Maya: good. Quick risk discussion: if we can't lock down the behavior we should pause the prod rollout. Any objections to that conservative approach?
[00:18:40] Jason: none, safety first.
[00:18:44] Priya: none.

[00:18:55] Maya: ok, final recap of owners inline: Jason (runbook + customer blurb), Omar (alerts + pager), Priya (telemetry + trace header), Samir (harness + heap profiles + release gating change), Ella (QA replication + seeds). I'll send the calendar note and update the release ticket.

[00:19:20] (short silence)
[00:19:30] Maya: any other business?
[00:19:34] Omar: small ask — include instructions in runbook on how to revert quantization toggles, there was confusion last night.
[00:19:42] Priya: I'll add revert commands and safety checks.

[00:19:55] Maya: great. Thanks everyone; we'll sync again tomorrow at 09:30 to check progress.
[00:20:02] (end of recorded excerpt — remaining discussion focused on task coordination and minor follow-ups)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard terms (K V cash), speaker overlaps, some metadata fields were omitted in crash path.
